40	## 1. Diagnose a server ("can't connect", "is it healthy?") — ✅
41	
42	**Frequency:** the single most common request (~34 direct, plus most ticket investigations). Representative: *"customer said they pointed their domain here but its not working"* (08-30), *"cant connect to this minecraft server cmuo7ajqt0rpohl44gj8triev"* (10-01), *"he says he still cannot connect, please do a deep audit"* (09-23), *"is everything running healthy after the reboot?"* (09-13).
43	
44	**Manual procedure (AI):** look up the row in Postgres → `qm status` / Proxmox API on the right node → guest agent ping → SSH in (password or management key) → `systemctl status <game>`, `docker ps`, `ss -lntup`, `journalctl` → `iptables -t nat -S NXEON_FWD` on the owning node (or via the node agent) → `nc`/probe from outside → `dig` A/SRV → check recent jobs → explain. Typically 10–30 tool calls and a few minutes per ticket.
45	
46	**Portal:** `/admin/ops/servers/<id>` → **Diagnose** (also embeddable via `ServerOpsPanel`). One ADMIN_OPS job gathers, in the worker:
47	- DB row + last 7 days of jobs (in-flight + failures), provision error/step;
48	- node API reachability, node CPU/RAM;
49	- VM existence on the recorded node, power state, uptime, CPU/RAM, `ipconfig0` vs `Server.ipAddress`, guest-agent ping;
50	- the server's expected DNAT rules (same `planNatRules` the real sync uses) vs the node's live chain (local iptables on the primary, node agent elsewhere);
51	- guest over SSH: load, RAM, root disk, failed units, OOM kills (24h), game unit + `is-active`, container restart count, last 80 journal lines → highlighted errors;
52	- join port bound inside the guest (any netns, same `gamePortBoundInGuest` provisioning uses);
53	- outside probe of SSH (banner) and the join port (TCP connect / UDP with in-guest confirmation) on the public address; flagged as *hairpin* when probing a primary-hosted server from the primary itself;
54	- subdomain A/SRV via public resolvers (1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8) vs `resolveGameServerDnsTarget`; customer's own domain A record.
55	
56	`lib/admin-ops/diagnose-rules.ts` (pure, unit-tested) turns that into a verdict (healthy / degraded / down / unknown), a headline, **ranked probable causes with evidence**, the raw checks, and **one-click fixes** through existing paths: start/reboot (`serverAction`), reconcile (`reconcileServerFromProxmox`), restart game service (`gamePower`), NAT re-sync (`SYNC_FORWARDS`), DNS re-sync (`SYNC_GAME_DNS`), retry provisioning (`retryProvision`), open the job queue, open guest logs. When everything is green the headline gives the exact connect address and says the problem is client-side.
57	
58	**Not covered / limits:** a true probe *from another node* needs a probe endpoint on the node agent (follow-up); today the outside probe runs from the primary. Per-server firewall rules are not yet evaluated rule-by-rule (the `blocked_path` cause points at them).
59	
60	## 2. Power: restart / reboot / start / stop — ✅
61	
62	**Freq.** ~32 (*"go ahead and restart it"*, *"reboot it"*, *"turn the free mc server back on on node 2"*, *"stop this vm, hes overdue"*, *"all servers need to be booted back up … if there is ever a restart"*).
63	**Manual:** `qm start/stop/reboot <vmid>` on the right node, or a DB-inserted job.
64	**Portal:** existing Start/Stop/Reboot on the server page (unchanged), Diagnose fixes, and **Bulk actions** (`/admin/ops/fleet`) with a concurrency cap (1–8, default 2) — the worker's `bulk_power` op releases the next server only when one finishes, skips (and reports) ineligible servers, persists progress so a worker restart resumes. "Boot everything after a node reboot" = Bulk → Start on all STOPPED servers of that node.
65	
66	## 3. Dedicated IP: assign / reassign / release — ✅ (same node) · 🔗 cross-node
67	
68	**Freq.** ~28 (*"assign the IP"*, *"give me a dedicated ip from the singapore pool"*, *"assign them both dedicated IPv4 address"*, *"just do the fucking transfer… is it attached to his server now"*, *"the IPv4 assigned to the node three test server was just a test IP … take that IPV4 and bring it over"*).
69	**Manual:** pick a FREE pool row, OVH/Hetzner vMAC, `qm set --net0 … --ipconfig0 …`, power-cycle, fix `Server.ipAddress/sshPort`, NAT resync, DNS resync, tell the customer. The older admin "release IP" button only freed the DB row and left the VM configured with the address.
70	**Portal (IP & placement card):**
71	- **Give IP to another server (same node)** — dry-run plan + warnings (downtime, billing), typed confirmation (the IP), reason. Worker `ip_reassign`: stop source → release (vMAC removed) → source onto NAT (new private IP + SSH port + game join forwards) → claim *that exact address* for the target (`allocateDedicatedIp(..., { preferAddress })`) → net0/ipconfig0 → power-cycle → restart source → NAT + DNS resync → notify both owners. The target is held by a HOLD job so nothing else runs on it meanwhile. Never auto-retried; each step idempotent.
72	- **Release IP (→ NAT)** — the correct version of the old release button.
73	- **Assign a pool IP** — first free or a specific FREE address on the node; checkbox for whether the add-on is billed at renewal.
74	- **Move to another node** — calls `requestVmMove` (stub until `feature/vm-node-migration` lands — that branch owns cross-node moves and IP carry-over).
75	
76	## 4. Ticket replies — 🔜 (stays with AI)
77	
78	**Freq.** ~26 (*"draft me a reply"*, *"give me ticket reply"*). Memory rule: never send without sign-off. This is language work, not an operation; the Diagnose result (headline, connect address, evidence) is the factual input a human or AI uses to write it. Canned replies already exist.
79	
80	## 5. Renewal price / billing corrections — 🟡 · 🔗 BILL
81	
82	**Freq.** ~20 (grandfathered price, add-on totals, "renew now", "his renewal price should be $8.99, next month 20% off"). Existing tools on the server page (grandfather price form, Renew now, Extend). The ops console links there and adds credit/refund/extend with reason + notification. Stripe/renewal internals are owned by the BILL workstream; nothing here edits `lib/stripe.ts` / `worker/billing.ts`.
83	
84	## 6. Migrate a server to another node — 🔗
85	
86	**Freq.** ~16 (*"migrate their server to node 4 … services, port forwards, dbs, files"*, *"move this customer's entire server onto node 3"*, *"migrate the free mc server to node 2 … porting, sub domains, DNS"*). Owned by the VM move engine branch. The ops console exposes it via `requestVmMove({serverId, targetNodeId, dryRun, reason})` (single server and from the drain planner); today it returns "engine not merged".
87	
88	## 7. Stuck / failed jobs — ✅
89	
90	**Freq.** ~16 (*"this apply game server settings stuff is stuck"*, *"im pretty sure its stuck, please wake it up"*, *"run the cleanup and restart the worker"*).
91	**Manual:** SQL on `Job`, sometimes restarting the worker.
92	**Portal:** `/admin/ops/jobs` — Active / Stuck / Failed / All views, per-server filter, live refresh. Re-queue (FAILED only), Cancel (QUEUED only), Force-fail (RUNNING only after 30 silent minutes) — each with a reason, compare-and-swap on the status, audit row. Policy (`lib/admin-ops/job-queue.ts`, tested): money-bearing jobs (RESIZE, DISK_EXPAND, ASSIGN_DEDICATED_IP) are never re-queueable (their failure is refunded); PROVISION goes through Retry provisioning; cancelling a DELETE un-strands the server (ERROR + note → Reconcile).
93	
94	## 8. DNS / subdomain / custom domain — ✅
95	
96	**Freq.** ~15. Diagnose compares public DNS to the expected target and offers **Re-sync subdomain DNS**; a customer-domain mismatch is flagged *customer-side* with the right value to give them (and the NAT caveat that a bare domain can't carry a port).
97	
98	## 9. Free server / credit / extend — ✅ · 🔗
99	
100	**Freq.** ~14 (*"apply the credit and send it"*, *"extend his trial by a day"*, *"Give Thorabin a Terraria Server… free for 30 days"*).
101	**Portal (Customer ops card, `/admin/ops/customers`):** wallet credit/debit (wraps `adjustBalance`), extend/shorten term (wraps `adminExtendServer` — gifted days never prorate into refundable credit), make free/paid (wraps `adminSetServerFree`). Reason mandatory; optional in-app notification and/or email (generic notification template). Granting a *game* server on a chosen node for N days is the partner-grant workstream (C); VPS grants stay at `/admin/grant`.
102	
103	## 10. Comp resource upgrades — 🔜
104	
105	Existing resize/disk-expand flows charge the customer; a "comp" (no-charge, renewal unchanged until next term) option needs a money-path change owned by BILL. Logged as follow-up.
106	
107	## 11. Tear down test VMs — ✅
108	
109	**Freq.** ~11 (*"tear these down minecraft-o3nu1n, minecraft-nsrtzj"*, *"Yes, destroy all 3"*, *"are you tearing down the old game test servers?"*).
110	**Portal:** Bulk → Delete, fenced to servers owned by staff accounts or accounts excluded from revenue (the owner's/test accounts); typed `DELETE <n>`. Leftover VMs without rows are handled by the drift scan's orphan cleanup.
111	
112	## 12. Refunds — ✅ (wraps `refundPayment`; card when traceable, else wallet).
113	
114	## 13. SSH / root password — ✅ diagnose · existing reset
115	
116	**Freq.** ~9 (*"I reset their root password… now it says I can't connect"*, *"is the ssh password the same?"*). Diagnose shows whether the *platform* can log in and whether sshd answers from outside; guest tool **SSH daemon** shows sshd state + recent auth failures. The owner explicitly does not want passwords reset as an automatic fix, so it is never suggested; the existing reset button remains on the server page.
117	
118	## 14. Node health / resources — ✅
119	
120	**Freq.** ~7 (*"what server is using the most resources"*, *"primary node is becoming unresponsive"*). Diagnose reports node CPU/RAM; guest tools **Top processes (CPU/RAM)**, **Largest files**, **Disk usage**; the drain planner shows committed-RAM % per node before/after.
121	
122	## 15/19. Orphans, drift, templates — ✅
123	
124	**Freq.** ~11 combined (*"do we have any free IPs that aren't being used by deleted or expired servers?"*, *"all ips that become orphaned need to be auto released to the pool"*, VMID reuse incidents).
125	**Portal:** `/admin/ops/fleet` → **Run drift scan** (worker `drift_scan`, read-only): orphan VMs (prod-tagged, no row — staging and untagged infra VMs never flagged), unmanaged VMs (info), missing VM, VM on the wrong node, DB-vs-Proxmox status mismatch, stranded PENDING/PROVISIONING/DELETING rows with no job, duplicate vmids across nodes, IP pool orphans/conflicts/mismatches, missing templates per provisioning node. Safe fixes only: destroy a **stopped** orphan (typed vmid; worker re-verifies tag/state/no row; `destroyVmIdempotent`), release an orphaned IP (refused if any server holds the address or a live DNAT targets it), reconcile status, diagnose.
126	
127	## 16. Logs — ✅ Guest tools: service journal, container logs, game unit status, cloud-init, kernel OOM.
128	
129	## 17. Transfer a server to another account — ✅
130	
131	Moves Server + volumes, websites, DBs, apps, cron, SSL to the new owner; invoices/history stay; optional root-password rotation; typed hostname confirmation; both owners notified.
132	
133	## 21. Node drain / rebalance — ✅ planner · 🔗 execution
134	
135	Pick a node → plan (drain fully or down to a committed-RAM target, same region first, 10 % headroom, largest first, dedicated-IP servers flagged) → "Stop new provisions" toggle (existing `setNodeAcceptsProvisions`) → per-move button calls the VM move engine.
136	
137	## 22/23. NAT gaps, restart game container — ✅ (Diagnose NAT check + resync; **Restart game service** = existing GAME_POWER, VM untouched).
138	
139	## 24–26. Resend emails, SSL reissue, Proxmox ACL — 🔜
140	
141	Low frequency and owned elsewhere (B adminmail owns EmailLog; SSL has its own flow; node ACLs live in Q's onboarding scripts).
142	
143	---
144	
145	## Safety model (applies to every action above)
146	
147	- `requireArea("fleet")` (ADMIN) for server/fleet ops, `requireArea("billing")` for money ops; refused while impersonating. Proven structurally by `test/admin-ops-actions-guards.test.ts`.
148	- Mandatory reason (4–300 chars) on every mutating op, written to `AuditLog` alongside the admin id and target.
149	- Destructive ops require a typed confirmation checked **server-side** (IP address, vmid, hostname, `ACTION <n>`).
150	- Remote work only in the root worker (`ADMIN_OPS` jobs); the web process never mutates Proxmox/iptables.
151	- Read-only ops (diagnose, guest commands, drift) never block on a wedged server job and run in parallel (`adminOpsLockKey`).
152	- Guest commands are a fixed whitelist with allowlisted, single-quoted parameters; output capped at 64 KB and scrubbed of the root password.
153	- Mutating ops are not auto-retried; each step is idempotent and re-runnable after a Diagnose.
154	- SANDBOX (`NXEON_SANDBOX=1`): diagnose returns a labelled simulation, IP ops swap DB rows only, destroys are no-ops.

Root: /opt/nxeon-wt-adminpages. Everything below is verbatim from the source.

## 1. Admin Ops

**There is no generic `<OpButton opId=...>` and no single `runOp(opId)` action.** Each op has its own typed server action in `lib/admin-ops/actions.ts` (`"use server"`). Each panel calls it directly through `useAction(fn)`, then polls the returned `jobId` with `useOpJob(jobId)` and shows `<JobProgress>`.

### lib/admin-ops/actions.ts
Every action returns `type Ok<T = object> = ({ ok: true } & T) | { ok: false; error: string }` (not exported). Private helpers:
- `gate(area: "fleet"|"billing" = "fleet")` calls `requireArea` and then `assertNotImpersonating()`.
- `enqueue(payload, serverId=null, extra?)` creates a `Job{type:"ADMIN_OPS"}`.
- `revalidateServer(id)`.
- `badId` uses `/^[a-z0-9]{8,40}$/i`.

Mutating actions call `cleanReason(reason)` and `recordAudit(admin.id, "adminops.<x>", detail)`.

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `getOpJob(jobId: string): Promise<OpJobView \| null>` | Poll an ADMIN_OPS job |
| `startDiagnose(serverId: string): Promise<Ok<{ jobId: string }>>` | Enqueue `diagnose` |
| `latestDiagnosis(serverId: string): Promise<OpJobView \| null>` | Last diagnose job |
| `applyFix(serverId: string, fix: string): Promise<Ok<{ message: string; jobId?: string; navigate?: string }>>` | One-click fix through existing paths: start/reboot via `serverAction`, reconcile, `gamePower`, SYNC_FORWARDS, SYNC_GAME_DNS, `retryProvision`, or navigate |
| `runGuestCommand(serverId: string, command: string, params: Record<string, string \| number> = {}): Promise<Ok<{ jobId: string }>>` | Enqueue a whitelisted `guest_cmd` |
| `restartGameService(serverId: string): Promise<Ok<{ jobId: string }>>` | GAME_POWER restart |
| `previewIpReassign(sourceServerId: string, targetServerId: string): Promise<IpPlan>` | Dry-run plan |
| `startIpReassign(sourceServerId, targetServerId, reason: string, confirm: string): Promise<Ok<{ jobId: string }>>` | `confirm` must equal the IP. Creates a HOLD job on the target inside `withServerJobLock` |
| `previewIpRelease(serverId: string): Promise<IpPlan>` | Dry-run plan |
| `startIpRelease(serverId: string, reason: string, confirm: string): Promise<Ok<{ jobId: string }>>` | Release the dedicated IP and move the server to NAT |
| `previewIpAssign(serverId: string, address: string \| null): Promise<IpPlan & { free?: string[] }>` | Dry-run plan plus free pool IPs |
| `startIpAssign(serverId: string, address: string \| null, billable: boolean, reason: string): Promise<Ok<{ jobId: string }>>` | Assign a pool IP |
| `requestServerMove(serverId: string, targetNodeId: string, dryRun: boolean, reason: string): Promise<VmMoveResult>` | Wraps the `requestVmMove` stub |
| `previewDrain(nodeId: string, mode: "drain" \| "rebalance", targetPct: number, allowCrossRegion: boolean): Promise<Ok<{ plan: DrainPlan }>>` | Drain or rebalance plan |
| `setNodeDraining(nodeId: string, draining: boolean, reason: string): Promise<Ok>` | Wraps `setNodeAcceptsProvisions` |
| `startDriftScan(): Promise<Ok<{ jobId: string }>>` / `latestDriftScan(): Promise<OpJobView \| null>` | Start a drift scan / get the last one |
| `startOrphanVmDestroy(nodeId: string, vmid: number, reason: string, confirm: string)` | `confirm` = the vmid |
| `startOrphanIpRelease(ipId: string, reason: string)` | Release an orphaned pool IP |
| `startBulkPower(action: string, serverIds: string[], concurrency: number, reason: string, confirm: string)` | `confirm` = `ACTION <n>` |
| `jobIntervene(jobId: string, verb: string, reason: string): Promise<Ok<{ message: string }>>` | requeue / cancel / force_fail, with compare-and-swap on status |
| `customerCredit(userId, amountDollars: number, reason, notify: boolean, email: boolean)` | Billing area; wraps `adjustBalance`, capped at ±$5000 |
| `customerRefund(userId, amountDollars, invoiceId: string, reason, notify, email)` | Wraps `refundPayment` |
| `customerExtend(serverId, days: number, reason, notify, email)` | Wraps `adminExtendServer` |
| `customerSetFree(serverId, isFree: boolean, reason)` | Wraps `adminSetServerFree` |
| `customerTransferServer(serverId, targetEmail: string, reason, opts: { notify: boolean; email: boolean; resetPassword: boolean }, confirm: string)` | `confirm` = the hostname |

`OpJobView = { id; op: string|null; status; step: string|null; progress: number; error: string|null; result: unknown; createdAt: string; updatedAt: string }`

### Pure modules
**types.ts**
- `ADMIN_OP_KINDS = ["diagnose","guest_cmd","ip_reassign","ip_release","ip_assign","drift_scan","orphan_vm_destroy","orphan_ip_release","bulk_power","hold"]`, with `AdminOpKind`.
- `isAdminOpKind(v)`.
- `READ_ONLY_OPS` = diagnose, guest_cmd, drift_scan.
- `AdminOpEnvelope {op, requestedBy, reason?, lockKey?, result?}` and the per-op payload types, unioned as `AdminOpPayload`.
- `adminOpsLockKey(job:{id;type;serverId:string|null;payload:unknown}): string|null`.
- `REASON_MIN=4`, `REASON_MAX=300`, `cleanReason(raw: unknown): string|null`.

**bulk.ts**
- `BulkAction = "start"|"stop"|"reboot"|"game_restart"|"delete"`, `BULK_ACTIONS`, `BULK_MAX_SERVERS=200`, `BULK_MAX_CONCURRENCY=8`.
- `BulkServer` type.
- `bulkIneligible(action, s: BulkServer): string|null`.
- `ChildState`.
- `nextWave(children, concurrency): string[]`.
- `bulkDone(children): boolean`.
- `childJobFor(action): {type:"START"|"STOP"|"REBOOT"|"DELETE"|"GAME_POWER"; payload?}`.

**ip-ops.ts**
- `IpOpServer` type.
- `IpPlan = {ok:true;steps:string[];warnings:string[]}|{ok:false;error:string}`.
- `planIpReassign(source, target)`, `planIpRelease(s)`, `planIpAssign(s, address: string|null, freeOnNode: string[])`. All return `IpPlan`.

**vm-move.ts**
- `VmMoveRequest`, `VmMoveResult`.
- `VM_MOVE_ENGINE_AVAILABLE = false`.
- `requestVmMove(req): Promise<VmMoveResult>` is a stub that returns "engine not merged".

**guest-commands.ts**
- `GuestParamSpec`, `GuestCommand`.
- `CONTAINER_RE`, `LINES_MIN=10`, `LINES_MAX=500`, `OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES=64KB`.
- `GUEST_COMMANDS: GuestCommand[]` (the whitelist).
- `guestCommand(key)`.
- `buildGuestCommand(key, params={}): {command; script}`.
- `capOutput(s, secrets=[]): {text; truncated}`.

**diagnose-rules.ts**
- Types: `CheckStatus`, `DiagnosisCheck`, `FixKey`, `ProbableCause`, `Verdict` ("healthy"|"degraded"|"down"|"unknown"), `DiagnosisFacts`, `DiagnosisResult`.
- `FIX_LABELS`, `STUCK_JOB_MIN=30`, `HIGH_PCT=92`.
- `evaluateDiagnosis(f: DiagnosisFacts, now = new Date()): DiagnosisResult`.
- `logHighlights(lines, max=6)`.
- `ipFromIpconfig(ipconfig0)`.

**drift.ts**
- Types: `DriftSeverity`, `DriftFixKey` ("reconcile_status"|"orphan_vm_destroy"|"orphan_ip_release"|"sync_forwards"|"diagnose"), `DriftFinding`, `PveVm`, `DriftInput`.
- `isTemplateVm(v)`, `vmTags(v)`.
- `detectDrift(input: DriftInput): DriftFinding[]`.

**drain-planner.ts**
- Types: `PlanNode`, `PlanServer`, `PlannedMove`, `DrainPlan`.
- `planDrain(opts:{...}): DrainPlan`.

**job-queue.ts**
- `JobLike`.
- `NO_REQUEUE_TYPES` = RESIZE, DISK_EXPAND, ASSIGN_DEDICATED_IP, PROVISION.
- `STALE_RUNNING_MIN=30`, `STALE_QUEUED_MIN=15`.
- `JobVerb = "requeue"|"cancel"|"force_fail"`.
- `ageMin(d, now?)`.
- `jobHealth(j, now?): "ok"|"stale_running"|"stale_queued"|"failed"`.
- `whyNot(verb, j, now?): string|null`.
- `serverStatusAfterAbort(jobType, currentStatus)`.

### worker/admin-ops.ts
- Registered in `worker/index.ts` as `ADMIN_OPS: adminOps`.
- Exports `adminOps(job: Job): Promise<void>`, which switches on `payload.op` to `opDiagnose`, `opGuestCmd`, `opIpReassign`, `opIpRelease`, `opIpAssign`, `opDriftScan`, `opOrphanVmDestroy`, `opOrphanIpRelease`, `opBulkPower` and `hold`.
- Also exports `gatherDiagnosisFacts(server, opts?)`.

These are private helpers inside ops, **not job types**:
- `moveToNat(conn, server, nodeRow): Promise<{ip; sshPort}>`
- `giveDedicated(conn, server, nodeRow, address: string|null, billable: boolean): Promise<string>`
- `powerOff`, `powerOn`
- `afterNetworkChange` (NAT + DNS resync)
- `releaseHold`
- `step`, `finish`, `failTerminal` (sets no-retry attempts)
- `notifyOwner`
- `audit(adminId, action, detail)`, a private writer that does `db.auditLog.create({..., category:"server"})`

SANDBOX is controlled by `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`.

### docs/ADMIN-OPS-CATALOG.md
It is not an id-keyed registry. It is a numbered list of 26 chores, each with a frequency and status (✅ shipped, 🟡 partial, 🔜 not built, 🔗 another workstream):

| # | Chore | Status | Where / how invoked |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Diagnose a server | ✅ | `/admin/ops/servers/<id>` |
| 2 | Power | ✅ | Existing buttons, Diagnose fixes, Bulk on `/admin/ops/fleet` |
| 3 | Dedicated IP reassign/release/assign | ✅ same-node; cross-node 🔗 | Destructive, typed IP confirm |
| 4 | Ticket replies | 🔜 | Stays with AI |
| 5 | Billing corrections | 🟡 / 🔗 BILL | |
| 6 | Migrate node | 🔗 | `requestVmMove` stub |
| 7 | Stuck jobs | ✅ | `/admin/ops/jobs` |
| 8 | DNS | ✅ | |
| 9 | Credit / extend / free | ✅ | `/admin/ops/customers` |
| 10 | Comp resize | 🔜 | |
| 11 | Tear down test VMs | ✅ | Bulk delete, staff/test-owned only, typed `DELETE <n>` |
| 12 | Refund | ✅ | |
| 13 | SSH | ✅ | Diagnose only |
| 14 | Node health | ✅ | |
| 15 / 19 | Orphans / drift | ✅ | Drift scan; orphan destroy is destructive, typed vmid |
| 16 | Logs | ✅ | Guest tools |
| 17 | Transfer server | ✅ | Destructive, typed hostname |
| 18 | Free deploy | 🔗 | |
| 20 | Bulk | ✅ | |
| 21 | Drain | ✅ planner; execution 🔗 | |
| 22 / 23 | NAT / game restart | ✅ | |
| 24–26 | Resend email, SSL, Proxmox ACL | 🔜 | |

Safety model from the doc:
- `requireArea("fleet")` for server ops, `requireArea("billing")` for money ops; refused while impersonating.
- A reason of 4–300 chars is required and written to AuditLog.
- Typed confirmations are checked server-side.
- Only the worker mutates remote systems.
- No auto-retry.

### UI
- **Pages:** `app/admin/ops/page.tsx` (overview with StatCards and tool cards), `servers/page.tsx` (search/list), `servers/[id]/page.tsx` (renders `<ServerOpsPanel serverId>`), `jobs/page.tsx`, `fleet/page.tsx`, `customers/page.tsx`. All start with `await requireArea("fleet")` and render `<OpsNav active="/admin/ops/...">`.
- **`OpsNav({ active }: { active: string })`** is a set of plain Link tabs.
- **`ServerOpsPanel({ serverId, sections = ["diagnose","guest","ip","customer"] })`** is an async server component. It gates itself and loads its own data, so you can embed it anywhere. Today only the ops page uses it.
- **Other panels:**
  - `DiagnosePanel({serverId, initial})`
  - `GuestTools({serverId, commands, isGame, gameUnit, running})`
  - `IpOpsPanel({serverId, dedicatedIp, sameNodeServers, freeIps, nodes, currentNodeId})`
  - `CustomerOpsPanel({serverId|null, hostname, ownerId, ownerEmail, isFree, expiresAt})`
  - `BulkPowerPanel({ rows: BulkRow[] })`
  - `DriftPanel({ initial })`
  - `DrainPlanner({ nodes })`
  - `JobQueueTable({ rows: JobRow[] })`
  - `ServerSearch({ defaultValue })`
- **`components/admin/ops/shared.tsx`** (client):
  - `useOpJob(jobId: string|null, initial: OpJobView|null = null) → {job, busy}`
  - `useAction(fn) → {run, pending}`
  - `JobProgress({job, busy})`
  - `ReasonInput({value, onChange, placeholder?})`
  - `Notice({tone:"ok"|"err"|"info", children})`
  - `PlanPreview({plan})`
  - `SectionTitle({title, sub?, right?})`
- **Confirmations:** there is no ConfirmDialog or typed-confirm component anywhere.
  - Typed confirm is an inline `<input>` that enables a `btn-danger` button when it matches (BulkPowerPanel), or `window.prompt` (DriftPanel).
  - Other places use `window.confirm` (`BulkTable` `action.confirm`, `ServerAdminActions`).

## 2. RBAC
- **`lib/rbac.ts`**
  - `Area = "overview"|"analytics"|"clients"|"support"|"fleet"|"billing"|"accounting"|"platform"|"redditTemplates"|"companyInbox"|"companyMailboxes"|"clientsBasic"|"supportTickets"|"liveChat"|"tasks"`.
  - `AREA_ROLES`: fleet, analytics, accounting and platform are ADMIN only; clients and support allow SUPPORT; billing allows BILLING.
  - `canAccess(role, area)` (ADMIN is always true), `isStaff(role)`, `areaForHref(href)` (default "platform"), `canAccessHref(role, href)`.
  - `requireArea(area: Area): Promise<User>` uses `realUser()` and **redirects** (`/login`, `/dashboard`, `/admin`) rather than throwing.
- **`lib/staff-grants.ts`**
  - `hasAreaAccess(user: Pick<User,"id"|"role">, area: Area): Promise<boolean>` (EMPLOYEE needs a StaffGrant row) and `hasAnyAreaAccess`.
  - `requireGrant(area)` and `requireAnyGrant(areas)` throw UNAUTHORIZED/FORBIDDEN.
  - `requireAreaOrGrant(area)` is the redirecting page guard.
  - Also `listGrantedAreas(userId)` and `GRANTABLE_AREAS`.
- **`lib/auth.ts`**
  - `realUser` and `currentUser` (React `cache`), `impersonating()`, `assertNotImpersonating(): Promise<void>`.
  - `requireUser()`, `requireAdmin(): Promise<User>` (throws FORBIDDEN if the role isn't ADMIN; based on `requireUser`), `requireStaff()`.

## 3. Audit, rate limit, idempotency
- **Audit:** `lib/audit.ts` `recordAudit(userId: string|null, action: string, detail?: string): Promise<void>`. It appends `actingAdmin=` when impersonating and records the client IP. The AuditLog model has `userId, action, detail, ip, category, createdAt`. The worker uses its own private `audit()`.
- **Rate limit:** `lib/rate-limit.ts`, in-memory and single-process:
  - `checkRateLimit(key: string, { max, windowMs }: RateLimitOptions): RateLimitResult` where the result is `{ok, retryAfterSec, remaining}`.
  - `resetRateLimit(key)`, `loginRateLimit(identifier)`.
  - `clientIp(source): string`, `UNKNOWN_IP`.
  - `claimOnce(key: string, ttlMs: number): boolean` (one-shot claim, idempotency-ish).
- **Idempotency / locking:** there is no generic idempotency-key helper. The closest pieces:
  - `lib/job-guard.ts` `withServerJobLock<T>(serverId: string, fn: (tx: Prisma.TransactionClient) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>` (pg advisory xact lock).
  - The in-flight-job count checks in actions.ts.
  - Compare-and-swap `updateMany` on status.
  - `lib/proxmox.ts` `destroyVmIdempotent`.

## 4. Design system
- **`components/ui/primitives.tsx`**
  - `PageHeader({title: ReactNode; sub?: string; children?})`
  - `StatCard({label: string; value: string; delta?: string; deltaGood?: boolean; spark?: number[]; sparkColor?="#8a70fb"; icon?; href?})`
  - `StatusDot({status: string; label?: string})` (maps RUNNING, STOPPED, QUEUED, DONE, FAILED, etc.)
  - `Badge({children; tone?: "brand"|"green"|"red"|"amber"|"slate"})`
  - `EmptyState({title; sub?; action?})`
  - `ComingSoon({feature; note?})`

It doesn't mark which are destructive; the destructive ones come from its safety notes on typed confirmations: IP reassign/release, orphan VM destroy, bulk delete and server transfer.
- **`requireArea(area)` redirects instead of throwing.** It sends users to `/login`, `/dashboard` or `/admin`. The versions that throw are `requireGrant` and `requireAdmin`. Ops use the "fleet" area (admin only); money ops use "billing". Both refuse while an admin is impersonating a customer.
- **Audit, rate limiting and idempotency:**
  - **Audit:** rows are written with `recordAudit(userId, action, detail?)` in `lib/audit.ts`. The worker has its own private writer.
  - **Rate limiting:** `lib/rate-limit.ts` holds counts in memory, per process. It provides `checkRateLimit` and `claimOnce`.
  - **Idempotency:** there is no idempotency-key helper. The closest are `withServerJobLock` (a Postgres advisory lock), checks for jobs already running on the server, and status updates that only apply if the status hasn't changed.
- **Two sets of UI building blocks and two kinds of tabs.** There are the older `components/ui/primitives.tsx` and the newer `components/admin/shell/primitives.tsx`. `SubTabs` tabs follow the URL, while `SettingsTabs` switches panels on the client and syncs a `?tab=` parameter.
